text: They landed on the far shore, in Gerasene territory.
As soon as Jesus stepped out of the boat, a man controlled by an unclean spirit came out from among the tombs to meet him.
He lived there among the graves, and no one had ever managed to hold him down, not even with chains —
he'd been shackled and bound more than once, and every time he snapped the chains and broke the shackles apart; nobody could control him.
Day and night he stayed out among the tombs and the hills, screaming and cutting himself on stones.
Catching sight of Jesus from a distance, he ran and threw himself down in front of him,
shouting, "What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Swear to God you won't torment me!"
(Jesus had already told him, "Spirit, come out of this man.")
Jesus asked, "What's your name?" "Legion," he answered, "because there are so many of us."
And they begged him repeatedly not to drive them out of that region.
Nearby, on the hillside, a large herd of pigs was feeding.
The spirits pleaded, "Send us into the pigs instead — let us go into them."
He agreed, and the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs; the whole herd — about two thousand of them — bolted down the slope into the lake and drowned.
The men tending the pigs ran off and spread the news through the town and the countryside, and people came out to see for themselves.
When they reached Jesus, they found the man who had been possessed by Legion sitting there, dressed, thinking clearly — and it frightened them.
Those who had watched it happen told everyone else what had happened to the man, and what had become of the pigs.
So they urged Jesus to leave their territory.
As he was climbing back into the boat, the man who'd been freed begged to come along with him.
Jesus wouldn't allow it. "Go home to your own people," he told him, "and tell them everything the Lord has done for you, and how he showed you mercy."
So the man went off and began telling everyone in the Decapolis what Jesus had done for him, and everyone was amazed.
Once Jesus had crossed back over by boat, a large crowd gathered around him again on the shore.
A man named Jairus, one of the synagogue leaders, arrived and fell at his feet the moment he saw him,
pleading urgently, "My little daughter is dying — please come and lay your hands on her so she'll live."
So Jesus went with him, and a large crowd followed, pressing in on every side.
In that crowd was a woman who had been bleeding for twelve straight years.
She had gone through doctor after doctor, spent everything she had, and only gotten worse.
Having heard about Jesus, she worked her way through the crowd and reached out to touch his cloak from behind,
thinking, "If I can just get my hands on his clothes, I'll be healed."
The moment she touched it, the bleeding stopped, and she could feel in her body that she was healed.
Jesus immediately realized power had gone out from him, and turned around in the crowd to ask, "Who touched my clothes?"
His disciples said, "Look at this crowd pressing on you — how could you possibly tell who touched you?"
But he kept scanning the faces around him, trying to find who had done it.
The woman, shaking with fear because she knew what had happened to her, came forward, fell down before him, and admitted everything.
He told her, "Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace, and be free from your suffering."
While he was still speaking, messengers arrived from Jairus's house saying, "Your daughter has died — there's no point troubling him further."
But Jesus overheard and told Jairus, "Don't be afraid — just keep trusting."
He allowed no one to come with him except Peter, James, and James's brother John.
When they got to Jairus's house, there was chaos — people weeping and wailing loudly.
He went inside and asked them, "Why all this commotion and crying? The child isn't dead — she's asleep."
They laughed at him. But he sent them all outside, then took the girl's father and mother and his three disciples in with him to where she was.
Taking her by the hand, he said to her, "Talitha, cumi" — which means, "Little girl, I'm telling you, get up."
She got straight up and started walking around — she was twelve years old — and everyone there was completely stunned.
He gave them strict orders not to tell anyone what had happened, and told them to get her something to eat.
